small_guidance:
- The conv-transpose kernel has IC=64 in a Python loop with one tl.load per ic; convert to a GEMM-style inner tile (BLOCK_IC=16 or 32) using tl.dot over [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_IC] × [BLOCK_IC, BLOCK_S] to use tensor cores. Sweep BLOCK_OC ∈ {32,64,128}, BLOCK_S ∈ {64,128,256}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3}.
- Autotune the GroupNorm kernel — current BLOCK_S=8192 with num_warps=16 is over-provisioned; try BLOCK_S=1024/2048 with num_warps=4/8 and cache x in registers across the two passes by tiling so the second pass doesn't re-load (or store ReLU'd x to scratch).
- Hoist the `w_off` computation and load the full weight tile once per (kd,kh,kw) outside the ic loop; precompute base offsets for input outside spatial loops.
large_guidance:
- Reformulate ConvTranspose3d as input-stationary scatter-add (gather form is fine since stride=1, but use it as an explicit im2col GEMM): for each (n, od_tile), do a single GEMM C[OC, S_tile] = W_mat[OC, IC*KD*KH*KW] @ Xcol[IC*KD*KH*KW, S_tile] using tl.dot, with kd/kh/kw enumerated via implicit im2col indexing (only IC is reduction-blocked, KD*KH*KW stays static_range). This will dramatically outperform the current scalar-per-ic loop.
- Fuse the ReLU and GroupNorm pre-pass (sum, sum_sq) into the conv-transpose epilogue: each program already produces a [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_S] tile, so atomically accumulate per-(n,group) partial sums into a small workspace, then a second small kernel computes mean/rstd and applies the affine. This removes one full read of the OC*OD*OH*OW tensor.
- Use channels-last (NDHWC) layout end-to-end so the GEMM-K (IC) is contiguous in input and channel reductions in GN are contiguous.
